sourceRecords.title: 15MW級浮体式洋上風力発電設備の基本設計承認（AiP）を取得
sourceRecords.sourceText: Tokyo Gas and Principle Power obtained ClassNK Approval in Principle for a 15 MW-class floating wind system using the WindFloat TC semi-submersible foundation with a central column. Tokyo Gas reports coupled turbine, floater and mooring analysis and basin testing against Japanese wind, wave and current conditions. This is design approval, not an installed 15 MW turbine or project procurement award.
sourceRecords.licenseNote: Public source; concise attributed factual paraphrase and provenance retained, not the full article. No broader republication rights assumed.

sourceRecords.title: Bidding Period Closes for 10 GW French Offshore Wind Tender
sourceRecords.sourceText: The AO10 bidding window closed on 12 October at noon. The French tender covers eleven offshore wind projects, including seven floating projects and approximately 5 GW of floating capacity within roughly 10 GW total. CRE confirms the closed submission phase and deadline. Bidder identities are not disclosed in the report; tender closure is not a project award.
sourceRecords.licenseNote: Public source; concise attributed factual paraphrase and provenance retained, not the full article. No broader republication rights assumed.

sourceRecords.title: The Celtic Freeport approves seed capital investment
sourceRecords.sourceText: Celtic Freeport approved GBP 18.4 million for four infrastructure projects. Floating-wind-related allocations include GBP 5 million for ABP Talbot Wharf, GBP 7.2 million for Criterion Quay at Pembroke Port and GBP 2 million for Ledwood marine access. A separate GBP 4.2 million supports business units. Awards remain subject to grant conditions and funding arrangements; completed infrastructure is not claimed.
sourceRecords.licenseNote: Public source; concise attributed factual paraphrase and provenance retained, not the full article. No broader republication rights assumed.

sourceRecords.title: New report reveals £14.6 billion opportunity for UK castings and forgings in offshore wind
sourceRecords.sourceText: OWGP and the Cast Metals Federation published a castings and forgings supply-chain assessment. It estimates more than two million tonnes of demand across UK offshore wind between 2026 and 2050, with up to GBP 14.6 billion GVA under its capability scenario. The scope includes floating-wind opportunities alongside other offshore applications; figures are report estimates, not orders or floating-only totals.
sourceRecords.licenseNote: Public source; concise attributed factual paraphrase and provenance retained, not the full article. No broader republication rights assumed.

sourceRecords.title: ClassNK Issues Approval in Principle for 15 MW WindFloat TC Design Developed for Japanese Conditions
sourceRecords.sourceText: Principle Power confirms the same 15 MW WindFloat TC AiP announced by Tokyo Gas on 13 October. Its statement identifies review of foundation and station-keeping responses under Japanese design load cases, including tsunami conditions. One approval event is counted, not two.
sourceRecords.licenseNote: Public source; concise attributed factual paraphrase and provenance retained, not the full article. No broader republication rights assumed.

briefingItems.title: Tokyo Gas secures ClassNK design approval for 15 MW WindFloat TC
briefingItems.oneLineSummary: ClassNK granted AiP for a WindFloat TC design developed by Tokyo Gas and Principle Power for Japanese conditions.
briefingItems.explanation: Tokyo Gas and Principle Power obtained ClassNK Approval in Principle for a 15 MW-class floating wind system using the WindFloat TC semi-submersible foundation with a central column. Tokyo Gas reports coupled turbine, floater and mooring analysis and basin testing against Japanese wind, wave and current conditions. This is design approval, not an installed 15 MW turbine or project procurement award.
briefingItems.whyItMatters: The announcement documents design verification for Japanese conditions while remaining distinct from construction and commercial deployment.

briefingItems.title: UK report assesses castings and forgings demand across offshore wind
briefingItems.oneLineSummary: A new assessment identifies manufacturing opportunities across offshore wind, including floating-wind components.
briefingItems.explanation: OWGP and the Cast Metals Federation published a castings and forgings supply-chain assessment. It estimates more than two million tonnes of demand across UK offshore wind between 2026 and 2050, with up to GBP 14.6 billion GVA under its capability scenario. The scope includes floating-wind opportunities alongside other offshore applications; figures are report estimates, not orders or floating-only totals.
briefingItems.whyItMatters: The report distinguishes current manufacturing capability from investment-dependent future potential.

briefingItems.title: Celtic Freeport approves seed funding for floating-wind port infrastructure
briefingItems.oneLineSummary: A GBP 18.4 million portfolio includes funding for floating-wind laydown, fabrication access and supply-chain facilities.
briefingItems.explanation: Celtic Freeport approved GBP 18.4 million for four infrastructure projects. Floating-wind-related allocations include GBP 5 million for ABP Talbot Wharf, GBP 7.2 million for Criterion Quay at Pembroke Port and GBP 2 million for Ledwood marine access. A separate GBP 4.2 million supports business units. Awards remain subject to grant conditions and funding arrangements; completed infrastructure is not claimed.
briefingItems.whyItMatters: The conditional allocations target port space and marine access; approval does not demonstrate completed construction.

The French tender covers eleven offshore wind projects, including seven floating projects and approximately 5 GW of floating capacity within roughly 10 GW total. CRE confirms the closed submission phase and deadline. Bidder identities are not disclosed in the report; tender closure is not a project award.
briefingItems.whyItMatters: The milestone advances the tender process without verifying winners, procurement awards or FID.

notes: Counts are the retained review inventory, not all search results. FOWT eligibility excludes opinion-only and unrelated floating nuclear coverage. No-candidate outcomes do not prove publisher inactivity.

Four independent developments were verified; the edition is intentionally not padded to five. Three use primary announcements, and France AO10 uses dated trade reporting with the older official CRE tender page as supporting provenance.
Tokyo Gas 13 October, Principle Power 15 October and Energy Global 15 October describe one AiP. Approval in Principle is not a turbine order, installation or full project certification.
CRE deadline on 12 October is an event date, not a newly invented publication date. The historic CRE page date is retained separately; tender closure does not verify winners or FID.
OWGP figures cover the wider offshore-wind sector, including floating applications. The resource page and news release differ on job estimates, so no job figure is repeated in briefing copy.
Celtic Freeport GBP 18.4 million covers all four projects, including a business-unit scheme. Floating-related port allocations are identified separately and funding remains conditional.

Carbon Trust IMRCI was excluded after its dated cover established 2 October and reuse restrictions were noted. No tender body was stored.
